official.deadline_note: The Foundation requires both the Mentor and Referee letters to be submitted by 15th November 2026, 11:59pm as well, and recommends that supporting letters be uploaded a few days before the deadline; no separate institutional deadline is published.
official.status_note: The Foundation's fellowship page states 'Applications Open for 2027' with a deadline of 15th November 2026, 11:59pm (IST); the opportunities overview independently lists the fellowship under 'Opportunities Currently Open' with the same deadline.
benefits: Monthly fellowship stipend for two years: INR 45,000 per month if the fellow is living and working in a 'X' category area, INR 35,000 per month in a 'Y' category area, and INR 25,000 per month in a 'Z' category area (final stipend amount at the Foundation's discretion)

Two years of support for self-directed work on issues of public importance under a mentor of the fellow's choice, with the chance to build a diverse worldview and establish long-lasting connections to issues of public importance
eligibility: The applicant must be an Indian citizen currently residing in India.
The applicant must be born on or after 1st January 1991.

The applicant must be a graduate (hold a Bachelor's degree) from a recognised institute/university in India, or, in the absence of a Bachelor's degree, carry at least three years of relevant work experience.
Those enrolled in academic studies/PhD for the duration of the fellowship are not eligible to apply.
Applicants proposing to work on art installations, photo books etc. are not eligible to apply for this fellowship; they are encouraged to apply for the Inlaks Fine Arts Award.
requirements: Complete all questions in the Foundation's Online Application System (OAS), entering name, address, latest contact information and other details correctly, and entering the Date of Birth exactly as per the proof of age and citizenship uploaded.
Statement of purpose and work plan must be completed in the Foundation's own supplied format and uploaded as PDF only; neither may exceed 1000 words.

The statement of purpose must briefly outline the applicant's personal and professional trajectory and the motivation for taking up the project and how it contributes to social change; the work plan must include a title of the proposed work, a concise description of the work or research, the expected outcomes, and in detail the manner in which the project will be undertaken with a clear timeline for two years.

Two supporting letters are required - a Mentor endorsement letter (describing the mentor's work experience and contact details, stating why the mentor endorses the work plan, agreeing to supervise the applicant during the fellowship, and indicating willingness to review and comment on quarterly and annual progress reports and to hold periodic meetings with the Foundation) and a Letter of Recommendation (elaborating the nature of engagement with the applicant and the reason for recommending the applicant and their work plan); each is uploaded by the mentor/referee through the link emailed to them.

The Letter of Recommendation must be from a person who has supervised the applicant's work for at least 6 months and cannot be the same person as the mentor; for fresh graduates, an academic letter of recommendation is acceptable. The mentor or referee cannot be someone who is currently an Inlaks Fellow or currently being supported by Inlaks under any other opportunity.
The fellowship is only to support individual learning and not for any organisational work; fellows must attend three workshops hosted by the Foundation at regular intervals.
documents: Statement of purpose and work plan, completed in the Foundation's supplied format and uploaded as PDF only, 1000 words maximum each
Mentor endorsement letter, uploaded by the mentor through the link emailed to them

selection_criteria: Two-round selection: a desk-review of applications, followed by an online interview of shortlisted applicants by a selection committee.
The application process is designed to assess whether the applicant's vision is aligned with the fellowship.
The fellowship is committed to supporting equality of opportunity, social inclusion, freedom of expression, and respect for individual and constitutional rights.
coverage: Monthly fellowship stipend for two years: INR 45,000 per month if the fellow is living and working in a 'X' category area; INR 35,000 per month in a 'Y' category area; INR 25,000 per month in a 'Z' category area - the final stipend amount is at the Foundation's discretion.
application_method: Click 'Apply Now' at the top of the fellowship page to access the detailed application instructions and the application form on the Foundation's Online Application System (OAS), hosted on Submittable.

Enter name, address, latest contact information and other details; for the Date of Birth field, scroll through the calendar or enter the date manually, exactly as per the proof of age and citizenship uploaded.
Describe the fellowship activity in a few lines in the 'Topic of your project' field, making sure it correctly represents the nature of the project.
Download the Foundation's statement of purpose and work plan format, complete it, and upload it as PDF only.

Enter the mentor's email address in the Mentor Endorsement field and submit; the mentor receives a link by email to upload the Letter of Endorsement (the field's default subtext mentions 'reference', so the mentor's address must be entered there).

Enter the referee's email address in the recommendation field and submit; the referee receives a link by email to upload the Letter of Recommendation - requests can be sent even before the applicant makes a final submission.
official.application_route: Online only: the 'Apply Now' button on the Inlaks Foundation fellowship page leads to the Foundation's Online Application System (OAS) on Submittable, where the form, statement of purpose/work plan and the mentor and referee letter uploads are completed.
official.study_mode: Full-time, self-directed two-year fellowship (individual learning only, not an academic or organisational programme)
official.citizenship_residency: The applicant must be an Indian citizen currently residing in India.
official.international_eligibility: No - eligibility is restricted to Indian citizens currently residing in India.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The fellowship project may take many forms, including action-oriented research, cause lawyering, grassroots journalism, ecological efforts, community rights, public health, and archiving, reviving, or reporting on dying arts, culture, language etc.; art installations, photo books etc. are not eligible (directed to the Inlaks Fine Arts Award); the fellowship supports individual learning only, not organisational work.
official.research_requirement: A work plan is required within the application: a title of the proposed work with a concise description of the work or research to be undertaken, the expected outcomes, and a detailed account of the manner in which the project will be undertaken with a clear timeline for the two years; the statement of purpose (1000 words maximum) must outline the personal and professional trajectory and the motivation for the project and how it contributes to social change.
official.duration: Two years, subject to satisfactory completion of a probation period (the first six months) and quarterly and annual review of the fellow's work; fellows for the 2027 cohort are expected to begin work from 1 May 2027.
official.description: The Fellowship gives young people the opportunity to build a diverse worldview and establish long-lasting connections to issues of public importance, encouraging them to challenge the status quo while building the confidence and security to explore alternatives and make independent choices about their lives. It gives graduates and early to mid-career professionals the chance to learn from a mentor of their choice and contribute to social change through self-directed work in India.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a two-year personal stipend for self-directed social-impact work in India, not a study award, so there are no tuition fees to offset and none are covered. The only published financial support is a monthly stipend of INR 25,000-45,000 set by the X/Y/Z category of the area where you live and work, so project costs, travel, equipment, insurance and any living costs above the stipend must come from your own pocket. Applications for the 2027 cohort close on 15 November 2026 (11:59pm IST) and your mentor and referee must upload their letters by the same date, so line both up weeks in advance. Shortlisting is announced by late February 2027 with an online interview within a fortnight, final fellows by late March 2027, and work begins on 1 May 2027.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Indian citizens living in India, born on or after 1 January 1991, holding a bachelor's degree from a recognised Indian institution (or three-plus years of relevant work experience), who want two years of mentored, self-directed work in fields such as cause lawyering, grassroots journalism, public health, ecological or community-rights work.
application_readiness_checklist: Download the Foundation's statement of purpose and work plan template (linked on the fellowship page) early and draft both to under 1,000 words, with a realistic two-year timeline and clear expected outcomes in the work plan.

Secure a mentor who will endorse your work plan, agree to supervise you for the fellowship, review quarterly and annual progress reports, and meet the Foundation periodically - and request their letter well before the deadline.

Line up a separate referee who has supervised your work for at least six months (an academic referee is acceptable for fresh graduates) and confirm neither the mentor nor referee is a current Inlaks Fellow or otherwise supported by Inlaks.
Enter both the mentor's and referee's email addresses in the Online Application System early so the upload links go out, and confirm both letters are in before 15 November 2026, 11:59pm IST.

Check your project against the stated forms (action-oriented research, cause lawyering, grassroots journalism, ecological efforts, community rights, public health, archiving, dying arts/culture/language) and confirm it is individual learning rather than organisational work with no art-installation or photo-book component.
Type your date of birth exactly as it appears on the proof of age and citizenship you upload.
common_rejection_risks: A project framed as organisational or institutional work rather than individual learning, which the Foundation explicitly excludes.
An art-installation, photo-book or similar art-practice project, which is not eligible for this fellowship (apply for the Inlaks Fine Arts Award instead).
Being enrolled in academic studies or a PhD during the fellowship period.
Naming the same person as both mentor and referee, or naming a current Inlaks Fellow / someone currently supported by Inlaks in either role.
A mentor or referee letter that misses the 15 November 2026 deadline because the applicant waited to trigger the upload links.
A vague 'Topic of your project' entry, or a work plan without a credible two-year timeline and stated expected outcomes.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Beyond the monthly stipend (INR 25,000-45,000 depending on the X/Y/Z area category), applicants must self-fund project costs, travel, equipment, health insurance and any living costs above the stipend; the published pages list no other coverage.
document_audit: The statement of purpose and work plan must use the Foundation's own template (download link on the fellowship page) and be uploaded as a PDF only.
Both documents are capped at 1,000 words each; the work plan needs a title, description, expected outcomes and a detailed two-year timeline.

The mentor letter must contain specific statements: endorsement of your work plan, agreement to supervise, willingness to review quarterly and annual progress reports, and willingness to hold periodic meetings with the Foundation.
The referee letter must state the capacity in which they engaged with you; both letters are uploaded by the mentor and referee themselves through emailed links, not by you.
Your date of birth must be typed exactly as on the proof of age and citizenship you upload.
alerts: The 15 November 2026, 11:59pm IST deadline applies to the mentor and referee letters too - send the upload requests as soon as you submit, ideally days before the deadline.
The Foundation states it will be unable to respond to individual queries regarding the status of your application.
Your stipend tier depends on the X/Y/Z category of the area where you live and work (per the linked government HRA classification), and the final amount is at the Foundation's discretion.
The fellowship carries a six-month probation period plus quarterly and annual reviews, and requires attendance at three Foundation-hosted workshops.

2027 cohort timeline: shortlisted candidates announced by the last week of February 2027, final interview within a fortnight, final fellows announced by the last week of March 2027, and fellows expected to begin work from 1 May 2027.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete the Online Application System form on Submittable via 'Apply Now', trigger the mentor and referee upload links by entering their email addresses, wait for both letters to land before the deadline, then await desk-review and, if shortlisted, an online interview with the selection committee.
